makingOf.title: How Saqi is built
makingOf.intro: Five short scenes: the design system, the water maths, the explanations, the tests, and who made it.

scene1.title: One file decides how it looks.
scene1.body: Every colour, size and motion in Saqi comes from design.md. It is checked against the Stylebase schema and compiled into tokens, so the water scale on the map is these seven lines.
scene1.caption: design.md · the colour block (excerpt)

scene2.title: Water first.
scene2.body: A block is watered only when tomorrow’s crop use would take it below its threshold, and only back up to its target. This is the whole sum for D-1, Khalas palms, with ET₀ at 5.8 mm.
scene2.note: The engine never rounds inside; figures round only when shown.

scene3.title: Every decision explains itself.
scene3.body: No black box. Each recommendation carries the reasons that produced it, in the order the engine checked them. These three come straight from the engine.

scene4.title: Tested like production.
scene4.body: The engine is pure functions under table-driven tests. The API and the web app have their own suites, and every change has to pass all of them.

scene5.title: Built by Husni Ramdani.
scene5.body: Built for a farm that doesn’t exist yet, to show how I’d build for one that does.

product.title: Four surfaces, one decision.
product.lead: The farm manager plans in the evening on a laptop or phone. The crew works the blocks in the morning. Both see the same plan, in their own language.

today.title: Today
today.body: The farm map, tonight’s schedule, the month’s water budget and what needs attention — on one screen.

block.body: Fourteen days of plant-available water, the threshold, every irrigation — and why tonight’s volume is what it is.

field.body: Tasks grouped by block, 56 px buttons, an offline outbox — in English, Arabic and Urdu.

making.title: Making-of
making.body: A scroll story of the water model, the design tokens and the tests behind every number.

decision.lead: A pure engine: no network, no clock, no randomness — the same inputs always give the same plan. Pick a decision to read the reasoning behind it.

instruments.title: Small instruments, honest numbers.
instruments.lead: Every figure carries its unit, its source and its age. Nothing on screen is decoration — if it moves, water moved.
instruments.budgetLabel: Projected {pct} percent of the monthly allocation
instruments.sensorLabel: D-3 sensor readings over the last 24 hours: the 30 centimetre sensor reports continuously; the 60 centimetre sensor has been offline since 12:00
instruments.footnote: Figures are the engine’s worked example for the fictional Farm 07 (ET₀ tomorrow 5.8 mm). In the app, weather and ET₀ are fetched live from Open-Meteo and every soil reading is simulated — the interface says so wherever they appear.

field.title: Built for bright sun, gloves and patchy signal.

targets.label: 56 px
targets.body: Every action is a big, high-contrast target — readable at noon, pressable with work gloves.

outbox.label: Outbox
outbox.body: No signal at the far block? “Mark done” queues on the phone and syncs when the connection returns.

languages.body: English, Arabic and Urdu. The whole layout mirrors right-to-left; numbers stay Western.

field.phoneDescription: Two phones show the Field companion in English and Arabic: offline with 2 changes saved, and tasks for D-1 and D-3, each with a large Mark done button.

making.title: How it was built, in three chapters.
making.lead: The making-of page tells the engineering story behind the plan — for anyone who wants to check the working.

tokens.title: One file decides how it looks.
tokens.body: Colour, type, spacing and motion live in a single design file and are generated into tokens. Nothing on screen is picked by hand twice.

water.title: Water first.
water.body: The water-balance model, built term by term with D-1’s numbers: from 68.0% today to 90.4 m³ tonight.

tests.title: Tested like production.
tests.body: A pure engine under table-driven tests, Playwright journeys across the three screens, and CI on every commit.

footer.disclosure: An irrigation decision cockpit for a fictional farm near Al Ain. A portfolio project — no real farm, client or company is shown.
